## Product and engineering direction

- Build a polished, premium, minimal portfolio, not a generic template.
- Dark palette: `#0B0C10` background, `#111318` secondary background,
  `#171A21` cards, `#F5F5F7` primary text, `#A1A1AA` secondary text,
  `#B6A0FF` accent and `#292D36` borders.
- Use readable typography, generous whitespace, clear hierarchy, restrained
  violet accents, subtle borders and rounded cards. Avoid excessive gradients,
  glow, animation, decorative icons and clutter.
- Responsive layouts must work on desktop, laptop, tablet and mobile without
  horizontal overflow.
- Use semantic HTML, accessible keyboard interactions, visible focus states,
  adequate contrast and `prefers-reduced-motion` support.
- Include page title, description, Open Graph metadata and favicon.
- Keep profile, skills, experience and case studies in strongly typed data,
  separate from presentation.
- Initial application is static: React, TypeScript strict mode, Vite,
  Tailwind CSS, Lucide React; Framer Motion is optional and should be
  restrained. Do not add a backend, database, authentication, admin panel,
  Docker, Kubernetes or Redux without a new explicit requirement.
- Target hosting: Cloudflare Pages (`npm run build`, output `dist`).
- No contact form unless separately requested; never place email credentials
  or secrets in frontend code or browser-bundled environment variables.
- Avoid unsafe HTML rendering and unnecessary third-party scripts. If a form
  is later added, use a server-side/managed service with abuse controls.
- Consider CSP, frame restrictions, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy
  based on actual site requirements. A passing build is not proof of security.
- Keep dependencies lean, commit the npm lockfile, and enable Dependabot and
  secret scanning where available.
- Consider Vitest/React Testing Library and Playwright as the app grows.
- Cloudflare Pages custom domain ruchabutala.dev may be configured only after
  confirming ownership and DNS access. Never request or store credentials.

## AI agent workflow

- Inspect the working tree, repository structure, package manifest,
  dependencies and relevant source files before editing. Preserve existing
  work.
- Implement only the requested phase; keep changes focused and follow existing
  project patterns.
- Never fabricate professional information. If a detail is missing, use an
  explicitly labelled placeholder or ask the owner.
- Use small, focused changes. Update directly related documentation.
- Run relevant lint, TypeScript checks, tests and production build after
  meaningful changes; fix failures and report any check not run.
- Use Git branches `feature/`, `fix/`, `docs/` and `chore/`; use small
  Conventional Commits when asked. Never force-push or amend a commit unless
  explicitly requested.
- Before pushing or deploying, inspect Git remotes, branch and working tree.
- End each implementation phase with changed files, commands run, verification
  results and remaining information needed.
